Night trains are back on the northern line
The overnight service between the capital and the northern coast returned this week for the first time since 2019, with two sleeper cars, a couchette car and a small dining carriage serving soup, bread, café au lait and local cheese until midnight.
Tickets sold out within a day of going on sale, and the operator has already added a second weekly departure for the summer. A bed in a shared compartment costs about the same as a budget hotel room, which many travellers said was the deciding factor.

The journey takes eleven hours, departing at nine in the evening and arriving shortly after eight the next morning. Staff on board said most passengers were families and older couples, but also a surprising number of students, who liked the idea of saving a night of accommodation.
Rail campaigners welcomed the return, but pointed out that the line still has long stretches of single track, which makes timetables fragile. A delay of twenty minutes near the border, they said, can ripple through the rest of the night.
